premises: Al has a strong negative enthalpy of mixing with constituent elements, driving segregation and ordering.
Al addition induces chemical ordering (short-range order) in multicomponent alloys, even in the high-temperature BCC phase.
Slow cooling provides sufficient atomic mobility for Al clustering and nucleation of an ordered secondary phase.
Rapid quenching kinetically arrests ordering, preserving the metastable high-temperature BCC state.
Al-rich clusters or short-range ordered domains act as precursors to long-range ordered precipitates.
